breakGlass.title: Emergency access
breakGlass.subtitle: For a patient who cannot consent
breakGlass.warnTitle: This opens a record without consent
breakGlass.warnBody: Use this only when the patient cannot consent and care cannot wait — not because a chart was refused. It is logged under your name, the patient is told, and a reviewer reads it.
breakGlass.noSearch: An exact Health ID only. There is no name search here, and never a list of patients.
breakGlass.lookupFailed: No record matches that Health ID on this server. Check it with the escort, the referring team or the patient’s card.
breakGlass.reasonHelp: In your own words. This is stored on the record, shown to the patient exactly as you type it, and read by whoever reviews the override.
breakGlass.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Unresponsive after an RTA, no escort and no ID; need allergies and blood group before induction.
breakGlass.reasonOk: {{chars}} characters — this will be stored and shown to the patient.
breakGlass.reasonShort: {{needed}} more characters needed. A few words is not an account.

ack.logged: This access is recorded against my name, this facility and this patient, and is marked as an emergency override.
ack.patientTold: The patient is notified — immediately, and again when they next sign in — and my reason is shown to them word for word.
ack.reviewed: A human reviews this afterwards, and repeated overrides on the same patient are escalated.

breakGlass.footNote: Emergency access opens the emergency profile only — identity, emergency contact, blood group, allergies and chronic conditions — and closes by itself after {{hours}} hours.
breakGlass.confirmBody: You are about to read {{name}} ({{healthId}}) without their consent. It is logged as an emergency override, {{name}} is told immediately and shown your reason, a reviewer looks at it afterwards, and it closes by itself in {{hours}} hours.
breakGlass.uncertainTitle: We do not know whether this opened
breakGlass.uncertainBody: The request got no answer, so emergency access may already be open and the patient may already have been alerted. Check your open grants before trying again — do not simply retry.
breakGlass.unavailableTitle: This server cannot open emergency access
breakGlass.unavailableBody: The emergency access route is not available on this deployment. Use your facility’s paper emergency procedure.
breakGlass.grantedBannerTitle: This access is on the record
breakGlass.grantedBannerBody: Every section you open under this grant is logged against your name as an emergency override, and a reviewer will read it alongside the reason you gave.
breakGlass.notNotifiedTitle: The patient has NOT been notified
breakGlass.notNotifiedBody: The alert could not be sent. The access still stands and is still logged — tell the patient or their next of kin directly, and report this to your facility’s governance team.
breakGlass.reusedBody: You already had emergency access to this record, so the existing grant was reopened rather than a second override created.
breakGlass.repeatBody: You have broken the glass on this patient before in the last 24 hours. This one has been escalated for review.
breakGlass.windowNote: The window is {{hours}} hours from when you opened it and reading does not extend it. When it closes the record is refused again, exactly as it was before.
breakGlass.noAllergiesRecorded: No allergies are recorded on this record. That is not the same as no known allergies — treat this as unknown.
breakGlass.scopeTitle: This is not the whole chart
breakGlass.scopeBody: Emergency access opens only what an emergency needs. Consultation notes, past visits, prescriptions and results are not included and are not missing — they were never part of this grant.
